q:
So here’s the deal- there’s a program in Spain I’d like to enroll my children in in summer 2027. This is a big deal- investment wise. 

My youngest needs to be potty trained to enroll.
cx: Child just turned two; a paid programme abroad requires training by three.

q: Am I foolish to think he can be daytime potty trained a year from now? My eldest was a breeze- one day at 2.5 told me she done with diapers and that was that. I hear boys are a bit trickier.
cx: Comparing with an easy first child.

q: We went out last night and the babysitter said he sat on the potty three times and did big pees. We are on our way! I definitely feel more confident starting to buy plane tickets and shelling out money for this trip
cx: A day later, after reassurance from commenters.

q:
I hate how stressed I was and feeling like literally everyone would have dealt with it way better.

Feel so awful and thinking how literally every person must think I'm awful too.
cx: Park trip with a four-year-old and a new puppy fell apart in the rain.

q: I've also apologised to my son, cuddled him and told him I didn't handle it well, and cuddled my puppy... but I feel rotten.
He doesn’t respond to us firmly telling him “no” he just thinks it’s funny. He also doesn’t really seem to mind when we take them away.
cx: Toddler drawn to every forbidden activity.

q: It’s becoming very frustrating and emotionally draining dealing with this kind of stuff every single day. Does this sound like behavior issues? Is he extra difficult? Or is this just normal “terrible two” stuff and I’m being a whimp?
cx: Asking strangers if this is normal.

q: I find myself caught in this weird middle ground where I'm trying to be the calm, regulated parent, but I can feel my own fuse getting shorter and shorter.
cx: Father of a two-year-old; post reads templated, twin of an earlier daddit post.

q: This is my first and only child so I am completely clueless. I only heard of „Oh Crap” method and Emma Hubbard’s (kind of similar). I know this time is kind of early but I also have heard that the longer one waits the harder it can get.
cx: Day three of Oh Crap block one with a 21-22-month-old.

q: when I know he’s doing his pee dance and put him on, he gets up right away, walks behind me and starts peeing…
cx: Mostly pees on the floor in block one.

q: We are at day 7 and it’s still hit and miss. Definitely better than the first two days with zero catches, now we get some successful ones (after naps), but still not well enough to move to block two.
9 weeks sounds like a long time though. I already feel so trapped at home..
cx: Reply to a commenter whose training took nine weeks.
